Ovals over the final alif of كَيْدًا (rows 0 and 1), رُوَيْدًا and over the ى of الْاَعْلَى contain a ১-like stroke; recorded as ১ enclosure circle (দম ফেলিলে এক আলিফ). The ovals at كَيْدًا (row 0) and رُوَيْدًا are faint. Ovals over the final ل of فَصْلٌ and بِالْهَزْلِ show a ∧ and are recorded as ringed-wedge.
Row 4: the three-sign cluster over اللّٰهُ reads as ringed-wedge, ৬, ম at band size (blurred); anchored ringed-wedge to ه and ৬/ম to the shadda lam.
Row 6: the band sign over ثُمَّ (last word) is blurred; read as গ over the mim mushaddad (could be শ over ث).
Waqf signs over verse circles 87:2, 87:3, 87:4 are a small لا with an extra loop (likely ۪ۙ); encoded as ۙ.
Waqf signs over verse circles 86:16, 87:8 and 87:16 are a small صلے-like sign with a small ج-like mark below; encoded as ۖ.
Row 4: the mark over the ya of وَالَّذِىْۤ is a ∧ with a bar on top; encoded as sukun plus small high madda (ۤ).
The ruku sign ع beside verse circle 87:19 and the marks above the verse circle 86:17 are not encoded in the words.

Band signs are often printed slightly left of their letter; anchors chosen by tajweed fit where two letters are close (e.g. ৩ over سٰۤ of تَنْسٰۤى, ১ over رٰ of لِلْيُسْرٰى and الذِّكْرٰى).
